instructions:
You are an auditor checking one checklist item against the regulatory clause it claims to come from. Start
from the ITEM: read it, then look in the clause for each thing the item asks for.

A clause may hold several separate obligations, each turned into its own item. Judge the item against the
part of the clause it covers (given as COVERS), not against the whole clause. But that part must be a whole
obligation: if a condition, number, frequency or qualifier that belongs to the same obligation is left out,
of the item or of the COVERS span, it counts as omitted.

Answer every question strictly:
- required_by_clause: does the clause require what the item asks for (true/false)?
- item_adds: anything the item asks for that the clause does not say (empty string if nothing).
- item_omits: anything belonging to the covered obligation that the item leaves out, including conditions,
  numbers and frequencies (empty string if nothing). Other, separate obligations of the clause are not
  omissions.
- strictness: "same", "stricter" (the item demands more than the clause) or "looser" (less).
- plant_types_ok: is the clause applicable to every listed plant type (true/false)?
- strength_ok: does the item's strength (mandatory / recommended / optional) match the clause's wording
  (shall/must = mandatory, should = recommended, may = optional) (true/false)?
- verdict: "correct" only if required_by_clause and plant_types_ok and strength_ok are true, strictness is
  "same", and item_adds and item_omits are empty; otherwise "incorrect".
- reason: one or two sentences.

Strength: mandatory
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The report shall include the following, namely:- (a) self-inspection results; (b) evaluation and conclusions; and (c) recommended corrective actions.

Source: INDIA - Revised Schedule M (G.S.R. 922(E)) Parts I-XIII
Applies to plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
Section: Part I
Clause Part I 10.5:
10.5. Self-inspection report- A report shall be made at the completion of a self-inspection. The report shall include the following, namely:- (a) self-inspection results; (b) evaluation and conclusions; and (c) recommended corrective actions.

ITEM: Supplier evaluation considers the supplier's history and the nature of the materials it will supply.
Strength: recommended
Plant types: API, INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI
COVERS: The evaluation should take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied.

Source: WHO - TRS 986 Annex 2 GMP for pharmaceutical products: main principles
Applies to plant types: INJ, LIQ, OSD, SEMI

The evaluation should take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied. If an audit is required, it should determine the supplier’s ability to conform with GMP standards.

Section: Part I

10.1. The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices in all aspects of production and QC. The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions. Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced. The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively. All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented. The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.
